title: during, for, while
subtitle: during the film / for two hours / while I was watching
summary: Learn when to say during (a noun), for (how long) and while (a subject and verb).

lesson.heading: during
lesson.text: **during** = at a time between the start and the end of something. It is followed by a noun.

examples.note: = at a time between the start and end of the movie

examples.text: We met some really nice people **during our holiday**.
The ground is wet. It must have rained **during the night**.

lesson.heading: in or during with time words
lesson.text: With 'time words' (the morning, the night, the summer etc.) you can usually say **in** or **during** with no difference in meaning.

lesson.heading: for = how long
lesson.text: We use **for** + a period of time to say how long something goes on. We never say *during two hours* or *during five years*.

examples.text: We watched TV **for two hours** last night.
Jess is going away **for a week** in September.
How are you? I haven't seen you **for ages**.
It rained **for three days** without stopping.

left.label: for = how long
examples: *A:* How long were you asleep? *B:* **For half an hour.**
We were stuck in a traffic jam **for two hours**.

right.label: during = when
examples: *A:* When did you fall asleep? *B:* **During the movie.**
Production at the factory was affected **during the strike**.

left.label: during + noun
examples: We met a lot of interesting people **during our holiday**.
Robert began to feel ill **during the exam**.

right.label: while + subject + verb
examples: I fell asleep **while I was watching TV**.
We met a lot of interesting people **while we were on holiday**.
Robert began to feel ill **while he was doing the exam**.

lesson.heading: More examples of while
lesson.text: **while** always introduces a clause with its own subject and verb. It can come first or second in the sentence.

examples.text: We saw Clare **while we were waiting** for the bus.
**While you were out**, there was a phone call for you.
Alex read a book **while Amy watched TV**.

lesson.heading: while + present for the future
lesson.text: When we talk about the future, we use the **present** after *while*. Do not use *will*.

examples.text: I'm going to Moscow next week. I hope the weather will be good **while I'm there**.
What are you going to do **while you're waiting**?

lesson.text: A quick test: if a noun follows, use *during*; if a subject and verb follow, use *while*; if it answers 'how long?', use *for*.

exercises.prompt: I went to the theatre last night. I met Sue ___ the interval.
exercises.explanation: The interval is a noun and we are saying when, not how long: during the interval.

exercises.prompt: The traffic was bad. We were stuck in a traffic jam ___ two hours.
exercises.explanation: two hours is a period of time - how long - so we use for.

exercises.prompt: Production at the factory was seriously affected ___ the strike.
exercises.explanation: during + noun says when something happened.

exercises.prompt: The president gave a short speech. She spoke ___ only ten minutes.
exercises.explanation: ten minutes answers 'how long?', so we use for.

exercises.prompt: Does each phrase need for or during?
I met Mike ___ I was shopping.
exercises.explanation: A subject and verb follow (I was shopping), so we need while.

exercises.prompt: There was a lot of noise ___ the night. What was it?
exercises.explanation: the night is a noun, so during (or in) is right.

exercises.prompt: ___ the festival, it's almost impossible to find a hotel room here.
exercises.explanation: the festival is a noun, so During is correct. While would need a subject and verb.

exercises.statement: Please don't interrupt me during I'm speaking.
exercises.explanation: Please don't interrupt me while I'm speaking. Before a subject and verb we use while.

exercises.statement: I was very tired. I slept during ten hours.
exercises.explanation: I slept for ten hours. We never use during to say how long.

exercises.prompt: Can you hold my bag ___ I try on this jacket?
exercises.explanation: while + subject + verb: while I try on this jacket.

exercises.prompt: You are going to Moscow next week. Put the parts in order.
exercises.answer: I hope the weather will be good while I'm there.
exercises.explanation: After while we use the present for the future, not will.
